hero.title_1: Born and raised in the 1st Ward.
hero.lede: Shakedia Jones was born and raised in the 1st Ward of Waukegan. She won nine IHSA state titles, graduated from Waukegan High in 1997, ran for UCLA and Team USA, and came home to build Furthering the Lives of Youth (FLY). Now she is running for 1st Ward Alderman.

hero.photo_cap: Dedication day on George Avenue, July 14, 2024.

story.lede: A girl from the neighborhood, a cousin who believed in her, and a city that cheered her on. Here is how Shakedia got from the 1st Ward to the world, and why she came back.
story.c1_p1: Shakedia Jones was born and raised in the 1st Ward of Waukegan, on what she calls the South Side. Growing up, money was tight.
story.c1_quote: My mom didn't have the money to pay for me to participate in any organized sports until I got to high school.
story.c1_quote_tr: Mi mamá no tenía dinero para pagarme ningún deporte organizado hasta que llegué a la preparatoria.
story.c1_p2: Then her cousin Shannon King, himself a Gatorade Illinois Player of the Year, talked her into going out for track. She called him "my angel."
story.c2_p1: In high school she won the IHSA state title in the 100m and the 200m all four years, plus the 400m in 1996. When she graduated from Waukegan High in 1997, nine was the most in Illinois girls' track history.
story.c2_p2: She was named Gatorade Illinois Girls Track & Field Player of the Year twice, in 1996 and 1997, and the Chicago Tribune's 1997 prep athlete of the year.
story.c3_p1: In 1998 she wore USA colors at the World Junior Championships in Annecy, France: gold in the 100m, gold in the 4x100m relay with an American junior record, and silver in the 200m.
story.c3_p2: At UCLA from 1998 to 2001 she was the 1998 Pac-10 champion in the 100m and the 4x100m relay, a two-time NCAA team champion (2000 and 2001 indoor), a two-time NCAA runner-up in the 100m and a multiple-time All-American.
story.c3_p3: In 2000 she was named to the U.S. Olympic Team for Sydney, in the 4x100m relay pool. She earned a B.A. in Sociology at UCLA, competed professionally after college, and later earned an MBA from Keller Graduate School of Management.
story.c3_photo_alt: A smiling selfie in a UCLA cap.
story.c4_p1: She came home to Waukegan for good in 2013. In 2014 she founded Furthering the Lives of Youth (FLY), an IRS-recognized 501(c)(3) with a simple mission: "assisting exceptional youth with limited resources."
story.c4_p2: Young people are nominated and need a 3.2 GPA. FLY has paid volleyball and track fees, bought equipment, bought a first cello for a young Waukegan cellist, sponsored a youth track club team and community track meets, paid for trips (including to Los Angeles), sponsored community trips to Chicago Sky games and co-hosted a backpack giveaway. More than 600 young people helped, by her 2024 count. She says she has helped 20 young people earn athletic scholarships.
story.c4_p3: She works for Waukegan Public Schools (District 60) as Family and Community Engagement Manager and has coached girls track at Waukegan High School. Titles are for identification only; the district does not endorse candidates.
story.c4_fly_note: Furthering the Lives of Youth is a nonprofit organization. It is separate from this campaign and does not endorse candidates.
story.c4_photo_alt: Young people and adults in FLY shirts at a park event.
story.c5_p1: Now she is running for 1st Ward Alderman, in the neighborhood that raised her.
story.c5_p2: She will bring the habits she has kept her whole life: set the goal, make a plan, do the work, and report back to her neighbors.

quote.text: I tell them whatever it is you do, make it your Olympics.
quote.tr: Les digo que, sea lo que sea que hagan, lo conviertan en sus Olimpiadas.

honor.lede: In 2024 her hometown honored her twice. She used the moment to ask the city to honor everyone else, too.
honor.d1_text: Waukegan dedicated the honorary street name "Shakedia Jones Olympic Way" on George Avenue, near her childhood home.
honor.d2_text: The City Council honored her with a proclamation. The room gave her five standing ovations.
honor.q1: Why isn't there a place where we can go to find out the people in Waukegan who have done amazing things,
honor.q2: ...so that people can see excellence from Waukegan.
honor.q_src: At the Waukegan City Council, August 2024
honor.q_tr: ¿Por qué no existe un lugar donde podamos conocer a las personas de Waukegan que han hecho cosas increíbles? ...para que la gente vea la excelencia de Waukegan.
honor.photo_alt: A group gathered at the Waukegan City Council ceremony, one woman holding a framed proclamation.
honor.photo_cap: Honored by the Waukegan City Council, August 2024.
